title: Language Model-Aided Text Semantic Communications for Digital-Twin Interaction
authors: Bo Chen; Can Wang; Chen Xu; Shuai Zhang; Huachun Tan; Liting Zhang
abstract: Reliable semantic interaction between physical entities and their virtual counterparts is fundamental to digital-twin operation. In challenging wireless environments, however, channel noise and fading corrupt continuous semantic representations, causing semantic drift, token substitutions, repetitive generation, and premature termination at the receiver. This article proposes LM-DeepSC, a language model-aided text semantic communication framework for digital twins. The framework combines end-to-end joint source–channel semantic transmission with a trainable continuous semantic feature adapter at the receiver. The adapter projects channel-corrupted features produced by the semantic decoder into continuous conditioning representations that a frozen pretrained language model can directly exploit. Consequently, the receiver jointly exploits residual communication evidence, contextual dependencies, and pretrained linguistic knowledge to reconstruct the source text without first committing to an error-prone intermediate token sequence. Experiments over additive white Gaussian noise and Rayleigh fading channels show that LM-DeepSC consistently outperforms DeepSC in multi-order BLEU scores and sentence similarity under the same transmitted channel-symbol budget. Evaluations over ten independent AWGN channel realizations further demonstrate a relative reduction of 46.3–71.0% in token substitution rate. On MASSIVE control instructions unseen during communication-model training, LM-DeepSC improves downstream intent-classification accuracy by 6.3–15.5 percentage points over DeepSC. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed LM-assisted receiver for robust text interaction under noisy wireless channels, with potential application to digital-twin systems.

title: Semantic Communications in the THz Band
authors: Fatima Ismail; Hadi Sarieddeen; Jihad Fahs
abstract: Semantic and terahertz (THz)-band communications are algorithmic and spectral enablers of future wireless networks. This work investigates deep learning-based semantic communication (DeepSC) over THz channels. We show that DeepSC models trained solely under additive white Gaussian noise generalize well to the tested THz block- and fast-fading channels when receiver-side compensation is applied. To enable fully data-driven reception, we propose a lightweight neural detector that does not require channel state information (CSI). At 0.3 THz, DeepSC outperforms a throughput-matched traditional coded communication system baseline over 0-12 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), achieving more than 50 percentage-point higher Bilingual Evaluation Understudy unigram (BLEU-1) score. The proposed pilot-free detector outperforms minimum mean square error (MMSE) equalization with both perfect and imperfect CSI and remains robust to frequency offsets up to 50 MHz, highlighting the resilience of semantic communication to THz channel impairments.

title: Where to Defend? Layer-Wise Adversarial Training for Robust Transformer-Based Semantic Communications
authors: Maria Slim; Razane Tajeddine; Mariette Awad; Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: Deep learning-based semantic communication (DeepSC), a Transformer-based encoder-decoder, achieves semantic fidelity over noisy channels but remains vulnerable to adversarial perturbations injected at multiple stages of the pipeline. We present a layer-wise robustness framework that compares fast gradient sign method (FGSM), projected gradient descent (PGD), and l2-normalized fast gradient method (FGM) defenses at the embedding output, and then uses PGD to analyze three attack and defense points: the embedding output, encoder output, and channel-encoder bottleneck. We evaluate reconstruction on Europarl and UK Hansard and sentiment classification on SST2 and YELP under additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Rayleigh fading. A first-order damage budget, {epsilon} times the l1 norm of the clean-input loss gradient at each injection point, predicts the attack-severity ordering, and the transfer matrix reveals asymmetric defense transfer: the embedding defense transfers strongly to encoder attacks, whereas encoder defenses degrade robustness against upstream attacks. For reconstruction, encoder-point training yields the largest matched gain but fails severely under embedding attacks; joint embedding-plus-encoder training retains comparable gains under encoder attacks while mitigating this mismatch failure, and Rayleigh fading attenuates robustness gains and degradation. For classification, three of four defenses collapse to constant predictors; only the channel-encoder defense remains non-degenerate, suggesting a protective role for the 128D-to-16D bottleneck. At a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 9 dB and perturbation budget {epsilon} = 0.3, the matched encoder defense recovers bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU) from ~ 0.10 to ~ 0.64 on Europarl/AWGN, whereas the mismatched encoder defense yields a -0.444 BLEU change relative to the undefended baseline under an embedding attack.

title: Image Semantic Communication with Quadtree Partition-based Coding
authors: Yinhuan Huang; Zhijin Qin
abstract: Deep learning based semantic communication (DeepSC) system has emerged as a promising paradigm for efficient wireless transmission. However, existing image DeepSC methods, frequently encounter challenges in balancing rate-distortion performance and computational complexity, and often exhibit inferior performance compared to traditional schemes, especially on high-resolution datasets. To address these limitations, we propose a novel image DeepSC system, using quadtree partition-based joint semantic-channel coding, named Quad-DeepSC, which maintains low complexity while achieving state-of-the-art transmission performance. Based on maturing learned image compression technologies, we establish a unified DeepSC system design and training pipeline. The proposed Quad-DeepSC integrates quadtree partition-based entropy estimation and feature coding modules with lightweight feature extraction and reconstruction networks to form an end-to-end architecture. During training, all components except the feature coding modules are jointly optimized as a compact learned image codec, Quad-LIC, for source compression tasks. The pretrained Quad-LIC is then embedded into Quad-DeepSC and fine-tuned end-to-end over wireless channels. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that Quad-DeepSC is the first DeepSC system to surpass conventional communication systems, which employ VTM for source coding and adopt the optimal MCS index under 3GPP standards for channel coding and digital modulation, in performance across datasets of varying resolutions. Notably, both Quad-DeepSC and Quad-LIC exhibit minimal latency, rendering them well-suited for deployment in real-time wireless communication systems.

title: Energy-Efficient Risk-Constrained Adaptive Semantic Communications Under Uncertain Adversarial Threats
authors: Maedeh Fallahreyhani; Paeiz Azmi; Nader Mokari; M. Reza Abedi
abstract: Semantic communication systems based on deep joint source-channel coding can provide task-oriented wireless transmission, but adversarial robustness may require substantial radio and receiver-side defensive-computation energy. This paper develops an energy-efficient, risk-constrained semantic communication framework under source-domain, over-the-air (OTA), and potentially composite adversarial conditions. Long-term total energy, including communication and diffusion-purification energy, is minimized subject to average semantic-loss, trajectory-level tail-risk, and end-to-end latency constraints. A recurrent primal-dual proximal policy optimization controller jointly adapts transmit power, semantic/channel bandwidth ratio, and purification complexity using causal channel observations, semantic confidence, imperfect attack-belief estimates, and recurrent history. A conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) constraint explicitly limits severe semantic failures. On CIFAR-100, at the unseen source-domain level $ε=12/255$, the proposed controller achieves approximately $61\%$ robust Top-1 accuracy with $\mathrm{CVaR}_{0.9}\approx0.36$ while using about $9\%$ less total energy than diffusion-only defense. At the unseen OTA level $Γ_A=-5$ dB, it achieves approximately $52\%$ robust Top-1 accuracy, reduces semantic tail risk by $40\%$, and consumes about $8\%$ less total energy than diffusion-only defense. These results demonstrate energy-efficient semantic defense under partially observable adversarial conditions.
keywords: semantic communication; semantic communications; task-oriented communication; semantic transmission; semantic channel coding

title: End-to-End Hardware Validation of OSSDM Semantic Waveform for 6G Communications
authors: Lahcen Attijani; Panagiotis Vlachos; Mohamed Amine Hamoura; Emilio Calvanese Strinati; François Rivet
venue: HAL (Le Centre pour la Communication Scientifique Directe)
abstract: Future networks are evolving toward semantic communications, where preserving task-relevant information becomes more important than ensuring bit-level reliability. Recent work introduced Orthogonal Semantic Sequency Division Multiplexing (OSSDM), a Walsh-based semantic waveform that outperformed semantic OFDM (S-OFDM) in simulation. However, its end-to-end performance over a real wireless link remained unverified. This paper presents, to the best of the authors’ knowledge, the first hardware demonstration of an OSSDM-based semantic communication system using a Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) X310 software-defined radio (SDR) at 2.45 GHz. CIFAR-100 images are transmitted through OSSDM and an S-OFDM baseline, and evaluated using classification accuracy as the task-level metric. While both systems achieve a similar Tx-side accuracy ceiling of about 76%, OSSDM consistently preserves higher accuracy after wireless transmission. These results provide the experimental validation that the robustness gains of OSSDM observed in simulation translate into improved task-level performance over a real wireless channel
keywords: semantic communication; semantic communications; semantic transmission

title: Adaptive Goal-Oriented Semantic Communication with Pretrained Semantic Encoding and Effectiveness-Aware Equalization for Beyond-5G/6G Networks
authors: Haseeb Ur Rehman; Kashif Bashir; Afzal Shah Muhammad; Suleman Soomro Muhammad; Umar Shahzad Khan Muhammad; Nouman Bashir
abstract: Semantic communication seeks to transmit task-relevant meaning rather than reproduce every source bit, but learned semantic representations can deteriorate sharply when they are perturbed by channel noise. This paper presents an adaptive, goal-oriented semantic communication framework that combines a pretrained Sentence-BERT (SBERT) encoder with a noise-conditioned neural equalizer. Text is mapped to a 384-dimensional semantic vector, perturbed by additive white Gaussian noise, and processed by the equalizer only when the estimated noise standard deviation exceeds an activation threshold of τ=0.05. A cosine-similarity rule then determines whether the recovered representation is accepted or sent for refinement or retransmission. In the reported embedding-domain experiments, adaptive equalization increased mean semantic similarity from 0.2475 to 0.6303 at σ=0.20 and from 0.0740 to 0.3545 at σ=0.70. The corresponding absolute gains were 0.3828 and 0.2805, respectively. At σ≤0.05, the equalizer was bypassed and produced no measurable change, avoiding unnecessary correction under mild perturbations. These results establish a proof of concept for noise-triggered recovery of pretrained semantic embeddings.

title: Semantic Communications: Principles, Architectures and Applications
authors: Sasa Maric
abstract: Conventional communication systems are designed to transmit data reliably, focusing on metrics such as bit error rate, throughput, and channel capacity. However, these traditional measures do not evaluate whether the received information is actually useful for a specific downstream task. To address this limitation, semantic communication has emerged as a promising paradigm that prioritizes the meaning, context, and task relevance of transmitted information rather than raw bit level reconstruction. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the theoretical foundations, system architectures, learning techniques, and evaluation practices in semantic communications. We classify existing state-of-the-art algorithms ranging from deep joint source-channel coding (Deep JSCC) and task-oriented feature transmission to generative diffusion models and contrast their operational trade offs against conventional baselines. Furthermore, we examine key application domains, including remote sensing, autonomous vehicles, and healthcare IoT, while addressing open challenges in security, privacy, robustness, and standardized evaluation.
keywords: semantic communication; semantic communications; task-oriented communication; semantic transmission; semantic channel coding; DeepSC

title: Recursive Code Evolution for Task-Oriented Semantic Communications
authors: Yan Gong; Zheng Chu; Wei Koong Chai; Hari Mohan Pandey; Jingrui Hou; Miao Zhang; Yuanjian Li; Pei Xiao
abstract: Semantic communication jointly optimizes inference accuracy, channel use, and computation, yet the underlying communication program is typically specified before training. This paper presents ComRSI (Communications-Oriented Recursive Self-Improvement), a framework for recursively evolving that program through large-language-model-assisted code edits. A fixed agent modifies the encoder, channel adapters, decoder, loss, and training policy; a protected evaluator screens candidates under prescribed budgets and resource constraints. Accepted code and textual feedback inform subsequent proposals, while candidate weights are trained from scratch. In the original ten-generation CIFAR-100 lineage, eight accepted revisions produce an attention-pooled code achieving 74.3% test accuracy over an Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) channel at 32 complex symbols per image, compared with 67.2% at 256 symbols for the initial design. The program also improves fading-channel accuracy and transfers to Tiny-ImageNet after retraining. A repeat study with ten searches per method compares ComRSI against non-recursive agents with and without textual history. Mean final search scores balancing accuracy, transmission rate, and computational cost are 0.7587, 0.7376, and 0.7089, respectively; the mean numbers of accepted revisions per search are 6.0, 5.0, and 2.1. The advantage over the memoryless agent is supported by a two-sided rank test, whereas the difference from the history-equipped agent remains statistically inconclusive at this sample size. Archived proposals show that pooling can yield a large improvement, while retained history supports subsequent refinement. These results support recursive program optimization within the evaluated setting and expose its remaining rate-robustness and compute-placement trade-offs.
keywords: semantic communication; semantic communications; task-oriented communication; semantic transmission; semantic encoding; semantic channel coding; DeepSC

title: More Interactions Make Communications More Efficient: A Directed Information Bottleneck Approach to Task-Oriented Communication
authors: Zhirun Zheng; Yiqin Deng; Phone Lin; Yuguang Fang
abstract: Task-oriented communication improves communication efficiency by transmitting semantic information required for downstream tasks, but may incur redundancy with previously transmitted information. To address this issue, we propose a variational directed information bottleneck joint source-channel coding (VDIB-JSCC) framework that transmits only previously unacquired information. Specifically, we use directed information to characterize the causal flow of task-relevant incremental information and theoretically demonstrate its advantages over mutual information and conditional mutual information. Based on this metric, we formulate a directed information bottleneck (DIB) objective that balances task-relevant information preservation and redundant information compression. We further derive a variational formulation, termed VDIB, whose tractable upper bound serves as the training loss. The encoder integrates a Vision Transformer for frame-wise semantic extraction and a Mamba-based causal state-space model for capturing temporal dependencies and extracting incremental information, while the decoder uses a Mamba-based state-space model for task inference. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 video streams demonstrate that VDIB-JSCC achieves higher classification accuracy with less transmitted information than state-of-the-art semantic communication methods. These results show that leveraging historical knowledge enables task completion with less information, improving communication efficiency.
arxiv_comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Networking

title: TwinViT-DeepJSCC: Adversarially Robust Semantic Image Communication
authors: Maedeh Fallahreyhani; Paeiz Azmi; Nader Mokari; M. Reza Abedi; Melike Erol-Kantarci; Eduard A. Jorswieck
abstract: Learning-based semantic communication is vulnerable to adversarial perturbations introduced before semantic encoding or over wireless channels. This paper proposes TwinViT-DeepJSCC, a preventive-corrective semantic image transceiver operating under a fixed channel-use budget. Two Vision Transformer (ViT)-based deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) branches learn complementary latent representations protected by sensitivity-aware masking. At the receiver, confidence-aware fusion, blind corruption-severity estimation, and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR)-severity-conditioned denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM) purification mitigate residual corruption without requiring attack metadata. Experiments on the Canadian Institute for Advanced Research 100-class (CIFAR-100) dataset consider fast gradient sign method (FGSM), projected gradient descent (PGD), natural evolution strategies (NES), and Carlini-Wagner (CW) source-domain attacks, as well as random jamming and channel-aware adversarial waveforms over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and block-flat Rayleigh fading. Under matched channel-use and attack budgets, TwinViT-DeepJSCC achieves maximum peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) gains of approximately 9.5 dB under 20-step PGD and 10.8 dB under channel-aware waveform attacks over block-flat Rayleigh fading. Under PGD, it also improves Top-1 accuracy by up to approximately 38 percentage points over the undefended baseline and 13 percentage points over the strongest competing defense. Ablation results confirm the complementary contributions of the proposed transmitter- and receiver-side mechanisms.

title: VQ-VAE Based Digital Semantic Communication with Importance-Aware OFDM Transmission
authors: Ming Lyu; Hao Chen; Dan Wang; Chen Qiu; Guangyin Feng; Nan Ma; Xiaodong Xu
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) significantly reduces redundant data and improves transmission efficiency by extracting the latent features of information. However, most of the conventional deep learning-based SemCom systems focus on analog transmission and lack in compatibility with practical digital communications. This paper proposes a vector quantized-variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE) based digital SemCom system that directly transmits the semantic features and incorporates the importance-aware orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) transmission to enhance the SemCom performance, where the VQ-VAE generates a discrete codebook shared between the transmitter and receiver. At transmitter, the latent semantic features are firstly extracted by VQ-VAE, and then the shared codebook is adopted to match these features, which are subsequently transformed into a discrete version to adapt the digital transmission. To protect the semantic information, an importance-aware OFDM transmission strategy is proposed to allocate the key features near the OFDM reference signals, where the feature importance is derived from the gradient-based method. At the receiver, the features are rematched with the shared codebook to further correct errors. Finally, experimental results demonstrate that our proposed scheme outperforms the conventional DeepSC and achieves better reconstruction performance under low SNR region.

title: Resource-Efficient Semantic Communication for Heterogeneous Agentic Teams
authors: Farhad Rezazadeh; Hatim Chergui; Lingjia Liu; Merouane Debbah; Merouane Abdelkader Debbah
abstract: Teams of autonomous agents, including large language model (LLM) agents, must coordinate over scarce and unreliable wireless links. We propose goal-oriented semantic communication (GOSC), a closed-loop co-design that jointly decides what each agent sends, when it sends it, and how reliably it is transmitted, based on each message's value to the team task. An edge broadcast of the team's common knowledge closes the loop by updating these values. We prove that a message is sent only if its value exceeds the cost of delivering it and that more valuable messages receive more robust transmission rates, and we show that the scheduler solves each scheduling step exactly whenever the radio budget is not saturated, which held in 95% of scheduling decisions. In search-and-rescue missions validated on unseen scenarios, GOSC meets the same mission targets as carefully tuned periodic semantic schemes with 1.2--8.5 times fewer uplink channel uses. In most settings, this advantage persists with realistic packet overheads, reaching 16.6 times fewer uplink channel uses and 13.8 times lower cost when downlink costs are included; in the rescue task, it also persists when all agents share one uplink. Rough value estimates suffice, whereas values that ignore message content can fail. With three different LLMs, GOSC uses 3.2--3.5 times fewer channel uses, while completion-time gains depend on the model.
application_scenario: LLM / Agent 辅助语义通信

title: Krum-Inspired Central Teacher Selection and Residual Channel Bottlenecks for Efficient DeepSC
authors: Rami Eid; Mostafa Jammoul; Omar Kaaki; Maria Slim; Mariette Awad; Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: Deploying transformer-based semantic communication models on edge devices requires compression that preserves semantic fidelity under channel variability. We study a compressed deep semantic communication (DeepSC) student trained by multi-teacher knowledge distillation and combine two ideas: (i) a residual channel bottleneck that splits the transmitted representation into a base stream and a residual stream with unequal power allocation, and (ii) a Krum-inspired, medoid-style centrality criterion that selects a single central teacher from a five-model ensemble, applied at the logit and intermediate-feature levels and combined with a feature-dominant distillation loss. On the EuroParl benchmark, a two-layer student recovers about 98% of the four-layer teacher's bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU)-1 under additive white Gaussian noise, with 93% of its BLEU-4 and 96% of its sentence-BERT (SBERT) score, and about 89%, 77%, and 87% of the teacher's BLEU-1, BLEU-4, and SBERT, respectively, under Rayleigh fading, while reducing non-embedding parameters by 1.33x and single-teacher inference latency by 1.79x (9.0x relative to a five-teacher ensemble used here as an upper-bound reference, not a deployment baseline). Controlled ablations over three seeds indicate complementary contributions of about +8.4% BLEU-1 (+9.6% SBERT) from the residual bottleneck and +3.0% (+2.9% SBERT) from centrality-based selection over mean aggregation. A decoder-mode ablation shows that the base stream alone recovers about two-thirds of the full BLEU-1 while the residual stream alone collapses, supporting the role of the residual as a refinement on top of the base.

title: Semantic-Aware Sub-Band Allocation for Terahertz Communications
authors: Fatima Ismail; Hadi Sarieddeen; Jihad Fahs
abstract: This paper studies semantic-aware sub-band al- location for terahertz (THz) communication systems, where frequency-selective molecular absorption creates highly non- uniform sub-band qualities. Unlike conventional formulations, semantic fidelity depends nonlinearly on the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and is also sentence-specific, leading to a non-separable assignment problem that is generally not solvable using simple ordering-based policies. To address this, we use a sentence-BERT (SBERT)-based surrogate model that predicts semantic fidelity from the sentence embedding and sub-band SNR. We propose an importance-aware scheduler that assigns sentences to sub- bands based on their semantic contribution using an oracle utility function that captures importance-weighted semantic similarity across sentence-sub-band pairs. A neural scheduler is then trained through imitation learning to approximate the oracle policy at more than 200x lower runtime than full DeepSC- based oracle evaluation. Integrated with a deep-learning-enabled semantic communication (DeepSC) system, the proposed method consistently outperforms all benchmark schemes and approaches oracle-level performance under realistic THz channel conditions.
arxiv_comment: Accepted for presentation at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026

title: SignDeepSC: A Semantic Signature-based Approach for Robust Semantic Communication
authors: Khalil Alhaj; Razane Tajeddine; Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: Semantic communication systems such as deep semantic communication (DeepSC) offer high efficiency but are vulnerable to adversarial attacks on their underlying neural networks. We address a physical-layer man-in-the-middle (MitM) threat in which an adversary injects perturbations into the transmitted signal to distort its meaning. We propose SignDeepSC, an architectural defense that achieves adversarial robustness without requiring explicit adversarial example generation during training. The approach is built on a perceiver-inspired semantic signature, a compact vector summary of the source features transmitted over a separate low-rate auxiliary channel. This signature is used by a self-repairing decoder that leverages cross-attention to correct distortions and can additionally drive a scrambler that shuffles the feature layout. We evaluate SignDeepSC over Rayleigh fading and additive white Gaussian noise channels under both single-step fast gradient sign method (FGSM) and iterative projected gradient descent (PGD) attacks. Under PGD ($ε= 0.7$), at 12~dB signal-to-noise ratio with Rayleigh fading, SignDeepSC achieves a bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU-4) score of 0.237 and bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT) sentence similarity of 0.646, outperforming all baselines without degrading clean-channel performance, when the signature channel is well protected.

title: AI-ENABLED SEMANTIC COMMUNICATION ARCHITECTURE FOR 6G NETWORKS: AN INTELLIGENT, CONTEXT-AWARE AND RESOURCE-EFFICIENT FRAMEWORK WITH HYBRID OPTIMIZATION
authors: Ganesan S.; Jagatheeshkumar G.
venue: International Journal of Science and Research Archive
abstract: Communication architectures that can enable intelligent services, vast connectivity, ultra-low latency, and extremely heterogeneous applications are necessary due to the sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks' rapid expansion. Large amounts of redundant data are communicated with significant bandwidth, energy, and computational overhead since conventional communication systems are primarily concerned with correct bit-level transmission. By conveying task-relevant meaning rather than full raw data, semantic communication overcomes this constraint. This research presents an AI-Enabled Semantic Communication Architecture for 6G Networks that combines context-aware decision-making, intelligent semantic extraction, and hybrid optimization. Gray Wolf Optimization (GWO) optimizes transmission parameters and semantic reconstruction quality, whereas Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) selects semantic features and allocates communication resources in the suggested framework. The optimization method is dynamically modified by a context-aware semantic controller based on network resources, channel conditions, and application needs. The framework is intended to maximize semantic similarity and communication efficiency while minimizing semantic distortion, latency, energy usage, and bandwidth utilization. Text-based semantic communication is used in an experimental assessment framework with different network loads and signal-to-noise ratios. For upcoming 6G applications, the suggested architecture offers a basis for resource-efficient, flexible, and intelligent semantic communication.

title: Secure Agentic AI and Multimodal Intelligence in 6G Communication Systems
authors: Satyam Gaba; Devanshu Motwani; Siva Sai; Vineet Suri; Vikas Ranjan; Vinay Chamola
abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) communication systems are expected to support immersive, intent-driven, and latency-critical services through tight integration of multimodal intelligence, edge computing, and autonomous network control. In this setting, agentic AI systems can reason over heterogeneous inputs, use tools and network functions, coordinate across distributed entities, and adapt to dynamic environments. These capabilities make agentic multimodal intelligence promising for 6G applications such as semantic communications, digital twins, and zero-touch network management, but they also introduce security and privacy risks that extend beyond conventional AI and network security models. Vulnerabilities can propagate across multimodal data pipelines, memory, tools, communication interfaces, and inter-agent coordination loops. We survey multimodal intelligence and agentic AI for 6G cross-layered communication systems from the perspectives of privacy and security. We present a 6G-oriented system view spanning perception, memory, tool use, and multi-agent orchestration; analyze threat models and attack surfaces across sensing, cognition, action, memory, and communication layers; organize existing attacks into a structured taxonomy; and review mitigation strategies including prompt and memory defenses, inter-agent trust mechanisms, secure orchestration, and privacy-preserving learning. We conclude by outlining open research directions for trustworthy multimodal multi-agent 6G systems.
application_scenario: LLM / Agent 辅助语义通信

title: QoE-Driven Hybrid Resource Allocation for Multi-User OFDMA Semantic Communications
authors: Xiaotian Xu; Zhifeng Tang; Guangchen Wang; Nan Yang; Xiangyun Zhou; Salman Durrani; Yansha Deng
abstract: In this paper, we develop a quality-of-experience (QoE)-driven hybrid resource allocation framework for multi-user downlink orthogonal frequency-division multiple access semantic communication systems, where the hybrid framework jointly handles continuous and discrete decision variables. Specifically, we formulate a mixed continuous-discrete optimization problem to jointly optimize transmit power, subcarrier allocation, and semantic decisions under coupled power and spectrum constraints. To better characterize semantic service quality, we propose a preference-inverse multiplicative exponential QoE that is bounded and non-compensatory, capturing the intrinsic ``both-required'' property of semantic rate and similarity. To solve the optimization problem, we develop a projection-based multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient framework that enforces feasibility for continuous and discrete actions. Furthermore, we integrate Gumbel-softmax relaxation with an adaptive performance-driven temperature annealing scheme to enhance the learning of discrete semantic decisions. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves superior convergence, greater stability, and higher QoE compared to the conventional QoE design and penalty-based or fixed-temperature baselines, highlighting the benefits of our QoE design and the effectiveness of hybrid decision learning in semantic communications.
application_scenario: LLM / Agent 辅助语义通信

title: Predictive Semantic-Aware Hybrid Automatic Repeat Request for Reliable and Efficient 6G Communications
authors: Osman KAYA; Muhammet Ali Karabulut; Can Eyüpoğlu; Oktay Karakuş
abstract: Hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) remains the backbone of link-layer reliability, yet it was designed for a setting in which every bit matters equally and the channel of the next slot is unknown. Neither assumption holds in semantic communication over time-varying channels: some parts of a message are decisive for the receiver’s task while others are not, and the deep fade that destroyed a first transmission is usually still present when an immediate retransmission arrives. This article proposes predictive semantic-aware HARQ (PSA-HARQ), a retransmission framework that makes its decisions at the level of individual semantic units and bases them jointly on how much each unit matters and on how the channel is expected to evolve. Semantic importance is extracted from a Transformer semantic encoder, a lightweight recurrent predictor forecasts the channel a few slots ahead, and a finite-horizon optimal-stopping controller decides, for every unit and every slot, whether to transmit, wait for a better slot, or abandon the unit. The forecast enters the controller through a confidence-weighted estimator whose weight is tracked at run time from the observed prediction errors, so that the policy falls back to the statistics-only optimum whenever the predictor becomes uninformative. Simulations over a vehicular situational-awareness task and over a real public record-classification dataset, with finite-blocklength coding and time-correlated Rayleigh fading, show that PSA-HARQ matches or exceeds the task accuracy of conventional HARQ in the low-SNR regime where retransmissions are most frequent, while transmitting far fewer blocks and consuming far less energy at the same channel condition. A cost-matched ablation shows that semantic importance and channel prediction contribute complementary gains. The results indicate that anticipating the channel, rather than merely reacting to it, is a practical and largely untapped lever for reliable and efficient 6G semantic communication.

title: A2SSC: An Agent-based Adaptive Semantic Speech Communication System
authors: Dongxu Yang; Fangyu Liu; Peiwen Jiang; Li Xiao; Shi Jin
abstract: Abstract In wireless environments with weak coverage or rapidly changing channels, reliable speech transmission is challenging due to fluctuating channel quality and limited bandwidth. Semantic communication offers a promising solution by focusing on the transmission of essential information rather than raw signals. Although existing semantic speech communication systems have made progress, they still lack decision mechanisms that are aware of both content and channel, limiting their robustness and flexibility. In this paper, we propose an agent-based adaptive semantic speech communication system (A2SSC). The system encodes textual content and speaker characteristics separately, and adaptively allocates transmission resources based on the importance of the speech content and the current channel conditions. At the same time, we incorporate an agent-based architecture to ensure system flexibility and scalability, and introduce an online learning mechanism that allows the system to continuously adapt to changing channel conditions after deployment. Experimental results show that A2SSC achieves comparable word error rate (WER) and speaker similarity (SS) to state-of-the-art baselines, while reducing the maximum num-ber of transmitted symbols by 62.5%. Moreover, the system maintains robust performance across varying channel conditions, demonstrating its effectiveness for reliable and efficient speech transmission in challenging wireless environments.

title: Covert Digital Semantic Communication With Movable Antennas: Constellation Shaping, Spatial Optimization, and Semantic Mapping
authors: Yunfan Bai; Yuwen Qian; Hao Jiang; Yiyang Ni; Feng Shu; Jun Li; Shuning Zhang
abstract: Digital semantic communication (SemCom) is emerging as a bandwidth-efficient paradigm for next-generation wireless networks by delivering the meaning of a source over finite constellations. However, the broadcast nature of wireless channels exposes transmissions to adversarial wardens, while discrete symbols deviate from the Gaussian signaling assumed by conventional covert communication. In this paper, we propose a covert digital SemCom system assisted by movable antennas (MAs), where the constellation, the antenna positions, and the semantic transceiver are jointly designed to conceal the transmission while preserving the semantic fidelity. Specifically, the maximum covert rate against the optimal detector with unknown noise level is derived in closed-form, which reveals that the legitimate signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) scales with the moment-matching order of the constellation and the spatial gain provided by the MA array. A Gauss-Laguerre ring constellation is then designed to raise the moment-matching order under the peak power constraints, and a covert symbol mapping with rank-to-ring assignment and scrambling is developed to carry the semantics in the ordering of the latent magnitudes. Guided by the derived semantic distortion bound, the semantic encoder and decoder are trained end-to-end through an invertible flow over the designed constellation and MA array. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme supports a higher achievable covert rate and improves the reconstruction quality by 24% compared to state-of-the-art SemCom schemes.
arxiv_comment: 13 pages, 9 figures. Submitted to IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications (JSAC)

title: Adaptive Semantic Communication with Residual Quantization for Resilient Vehicular Networks
authors: Xuanhao Luo; Ruichen Gao; Sandeep Sreenivasan; Zhizhen Li; Yuchen Liu
abstract: Vehicular networks require timely visual information exchange to support safety-critical applications such as cooperative perception and hazard awareness, yet transmitting high-dimensional camera data over bandwidth-limited and dynamic wireless links remains challenging. In this paper, we propose an adaptive semantic communication architecture for vehicular multicast that adjusts the amount of visual information transmitted according to current channel conditions, available communication resources, and latency requirements. Specifically, the visual encoder uses residual quantization to represent each image at multiple bitrate and reconstruction-quality levels. At runtime, the system selects an appropriate level based on the communication conditions, enabling it to trade visual fidelity for lower transmission overhead when network resources are limited. Context-adaptive entropy coding further compresses the quantized representations using offline-learned statistics, without requiring retraining for different channel conditions. This design allows the visual representation to be learned offline while the communication strategy is adapted online. Experimental results demonstrate competitive rate-distortion performance at ultra-low bitrates, improved delivery reliability and deadline satisfaction across diverse vehicular scenarios, and strong downstream perception performance, achieving up to 0.88 mAP50 while dynamically adapting to changing communication conditions.

title: 6G Semantic Intelligence for UAV Anti Jamming: A Transformer Augmented Predictive Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework
authors: Le Hoang Hiep; Ngo Huu-Huy
venue: VNU Journal of Science Computer Science and Communication Engineering
abstract: This paper proposes a semantic-aware predictive hybrid Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) framework for UAV anti-jamming communications under partial observability and nonstationary interference. The framework integrates Transformer-based channel-wise interference prediction, adaptive semantic-rate control, energy-aware horizontal UAV mobility, and hierarchicaldiscrete–continuous control within a unified POMDP. The semantic payload is explicitly coupledwith achievable rate, transmission duration, delivery success, and propulsion–communication energy,while predictor learning is separated from the on-policy PPO update. Evaluation over 50 independenttrials shows that, at a jammer power of 30 dBm and CSI error variance of 10-3, the proposed methodachieves a semantic accuracy of 0.751 ± 0.005, a task-success rate of 0.715 ± 0.007, and an SINRof 6.48 ± 0.28 dB, while consuming 23.58 ± 0.20 J/slot. The closest LSTM-Hybrid PPO baselineobtains 0.694±0.006, 0.642±0.006, 5.37±0.26 dB, and 25.46±0.17 J/slot, respectively. The Transformer predictor achieves an RMSE of approximately 0.039 under perfect CSI and 0.091 at a CSIerror variance of 10-2. Under an unseen jammer-policy shift, online predictor adaptation recoverssemantic accuracy to approximately 0.859, compared with 0.746 for a frozen predictor. Ablation results indicate complementary contributions from prediction, semantic-rate adaptation, mobility, andhierarchical hybrid control.Keywords: Deep Reinforcement Learning, Predictive Anti-Jamming, Semantic Communication,Transformer-Based Prediction, UAV Networks. 04:28:10 dblclick "Deep Reinforcement Learning, Predictive Anti-Jamming, Semantic Communication, Transformer-Based Prediction, UAV Networks." sidepanelOpen=false autoUpdate=true isAdv=true

title: RetinaSC: Retinal Semantic Communication Framework for Diabetic Retinopathy Detection
authors: Avani Shinod; Rangineni Rushitha; Asqeem Nas; Anirban Bhowal; Shikha Baghel
abstract: This paper presents a lightweight semantic com- munication framework for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading from fundus images pertaining specifically to the APTOS2019 dataset. The framework includes semantic encoder designed using ResNet34, U-Net, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNet-B0 architectures. Further, the trained models are used to train the same framework for IDRiD dataset using transfer learning approach. Such a framework will enable the telemedicine sector in the early detection of DR and prevent total blindness. The results reveal that for APTOS, task-oriented semantic systems can achieve satisfactory robust performance (more than 0.8 weighted F1 score for ResNet34 and EfficientNet-B0) across different channels. In particular, considering the trade-off between complexity, latency, throughput, and F1 score, MobileNetV2 is the best model with weighted F1 score of 0.76-0.78 for both task and reconstruction- oriented modules and end-to-end latency of only 8.162 ms.

title: Semantic Edge-Cloud Communication for Real-Time Urban Traffic Digital Twins
authors: Murat Arda Onsu; Arman Dogru; Poonam Lohan; Burak Kantarci; Aisha Syed
abstract: Urban traffic systems are becoming increasingly complex, demanding real-time traffic perception, proactive collision prediction, and intelligent management to improve safety and reduce congestion. Although AI-driven traffic management has shown strong promise, its success relies on diverse, high-quality data spanning critical scenarios such as collisions, near-collisions, and traffic rule violations. Digital twins offer a powerful solution by enabling synchronized virtual replicas of physical traffic environments for real-time monitoring, collision prediction, traffic-flow optimization, and diverse realistic scenario generation. However, continuously synchronizing a high-fidelity urban traffic digital twin through edge surveillance cameras requires substantial edge-cloud communication, and transmitting raw video streams leads to severe bandwidth and latency constraints. To overcome this challenge, this paper proposes a semantic communication-based edge-cloud framework for real-time urban traffic digital twin applications. By leveraging edge intelligence to extract and transmit only task-relevant semantic traffic information instead of full video feeds, the proposed framework significantly reduces communication overhead while preserving the essential dynamics needed for accurate real-time digital twin reconstruction. Experimental results demonstrate more than 99% transmission savings and an average trajectory reconstruction error of only 0.12 m, confirming the proposed framework as an effective, scalable, and low-latency solution for AI-enabled urban traffic digital twin applications.

title: Beyond Task Relevance: Interaction-Aware Semantic Communication for Wireless Agent Collaboration
authors: Yiru Wang; Pengxin Guan; Xiumei Deng; Zehui Xiong
abstract: Semantic communication in multi-agent systems often assumes that task-relevant information benefits the team once delivered. Yet semantic sharing can alter the receiver's decision and increase inter-agent dependence, potentially reducing team utility. Motivated by this phenomenon, we develop an interaction-aware framework for wireless collaboration between heterogeneous agents. We analytically relate communication-induced dependence to expected best-of-team utility and define a team-level semantic value for candidate messages. We consider semantic units at different abstraction levels and formulate a deadline- and power-constrained problem that maximizes predicted team-level net surplus. We derive an interaction-aware policy that selects at most one unit and its transmit power, or chooses not to transmit. Experiments on two verifier-scored optimization tasks show that full-solution exchange induces stronger structural convergence and more adverse team-level effects, whereas method hints exhibit pronounced directionality. Across the evaluated power budgets, our policy achieves the highest net team-level surplus while consuming less energy than semantic-aware and full-solution baselines.
keywords: semantic communication; semantic communications; semantic-aware communication
application_scenario: LLM / Agent 辅助语义通信

title: Cryptographically Secure Agent-to-Agent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Karol Budzyn; Adrian Brodzik; Mateusz Szczepkowski
abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) comprise AI agents that collaborate or compete to perform complex, distributed tasks. Their dynamic interactions create opportunities for threat actors to target and impersonate other agents, intercept messages, inject malicious prompts, and exfiltrate sensitive data while simultaneously complicating the detection of anomalous behavior through conventional monitoring. This paper surveys threats and cryptographic challenges in agent-to-agent communication and presents a zero-trust architecture integrating identity, transport security, message integrity, and monitoring. The architecture establishes agent identities via decentralized identifiers and task-scoped verifiable credentials backed by a permissioned ledger, enforcing least-privilege authorization. For transport security, it provides mutually authenticated, crypto-agile TLS with hybrid post-quantum key establishment, and evaluates KEMTLS with pre-distributed public keys to reduce handshake overhead. Signed CBOR envelopes preserve payload integrity across multi-hop exchanges, while zero-knowledge proofs verify declared task constraints without exposing underlying inputs. Context-aware monitoring of inter-agent messages, tool activity, and execution telemetry informs the setting of risk-based trust thresholds and supports the detection of behavioral anomalies. Together, these mechanisms provide an integrated framework for securing and auditing agent communication, with implications for other agentic protocols and prospective 6G semantic communication.
application_scenario: LLM / Agent 辅助语义通信

title: Adaptive Role Assignment and Controlled Feature Reconstruction for Federated Image Semantic Communication
authors: Yuxuan Chen; Jiao Bie; Hang Qi; Jingjin Wu
abstract: Hybrid federated semantic communication enables user equipment (UEs) to contribute model updates or semantic features under a shared training framework. However, heterogeneous role costs and the interaction between model aggregation and feature reconstruction (FR) remain key challenges in practical radio access network (RAN) deployment. To address these issues, we propose ARC-FedSC, a RAN-aware framework that coordinates UE role assignment and server-side controlled FR under a fixed communication budget. Within ARC-FedSC, RAN Aware Role-Bandit learns the historical contribution of UEs in different roles together with current uplink conditions, while Temporal Consistency Alignment (TCA) regulates FR according to recent model aggregation directions. Experiments on CIFAR-10 with time-varying RAN channels show that ARC-FedSC outperforms baselines across all five tested role configurations in the later training stage, with the best configurations achieving about 24.17 dB average PSNR over the last 20 rounds. Component level results further show that Role-Bandit maintains an average rolling UE coverage of 85.3%, compared with about 65.7% for baseline, while TCA reduces the probability of harmful FR events from 0.245 to 0.093, corresponding to a 62.0% reduction. Ablation and sensitivity studies further support the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed design.

title: Receiver-Specific Interventional Valuation of Semantic Atoms for Budget-Constrained Multi-Agent Communication
authors: Danial Dehghani; Maximilian Lübke; Friedemann Laue; Zahra Seifaei; Norman Franchi
abstract: Cooperative multi-agent semantic communication requires deciding not only how a transmitter encodes its observation, but also which resulting semantic content should be delivered to each receiver under a limited link budget. We introduce an encoder-agnostic transmitter-side framework for receiver-specific valuation of independently selectable semantic units, termed semantic atoms. Each atom is assigned a signed value that quantifies whether delivering it is expected to improve or degrade the intended receiver's downstream decision. We formulate this effect through a controlled-delivery utility and identify it via prospective randomized payload delivery before the receiver acts. A shadow receiver estimates this utility using only transmitter-available information, from which receiver-specific leave-one-out (LOO) and Shapley atom values are computed. Experiments on a four-receiver intersection benchmark show 68.4% accuracy in recovering the sign of non-negligible LOO atom effects and a Spearman correlation of 0.302 between estimated and reference LOO values. Under limited budgets, we show that receiver-specific selection consistently outperforms shared and random alternatives, demonstrating the benefit of adapting semantic ranking to the intended receiver. At full affordability, exhaustive subset selection also outperforms full-payload transmission, showing that transmitting all available content need not maximize receiver utility. Overall, our results show that receiver-specific semantic valuation can support effective budget-constrained communication despite imperfect atom-value estimation.
application_scenario: LLM / Agent 辅助语义通信
